subject: Why does inla.group.cv() return NA for some zero-inflated Poisson models?

messages.author: d3ed03796f3ab15b
messages.subject: Why does inla.group.cv() return NA for some zero-inflated Poisson models?
parts:
Hi ,
I'm working on evaluating the predictive performance of spatio-temporal models when the proportion of zeros in the data is high.

I've tested several models (Poisson, zeroinflatedpoisson1, and zeroinflatedpoisson0) each without and with an interaction (Type I).

According to the WAIC criterion, the best model is:

bym2.rw2.iid_intI_iid.base <- inla(formula.bym2.rw2.iid_intI_iid,
                                   family=family,data=map,E=E,verbose = TRUE,
                                   control.compute = control.compute, control.inla = control.inla)

Next, I attempted to implement the U(LGOCV) approach using the grouping structure from this selected model

gcpo.default.3.base <- inla.group.cv(bym2.rw2.iid_intI_iid.base, num.level.sets = 3, strategy = "posterior")
gcpo.ZIP1.bym2..iid.base<- inla.group.cv(ZIP1.bym2..iid.base , group.cv = gcpo.default.3.base)
gcpo.ZIP0.bym2..iid.base<- inla.group.cv(ZIP0.bym2..iid.base , group.cv = gcpo.default.3.base)
gcpo.ZIP1.bym2.rw2.base<- inla.group.cv(ZIP1.bym2.rw2.base , group.cv = gcpo.default.3.base)
gcpo.ZIP0.bym2.rw2.base<- inla.group.cv(ZIP0.bym2.rw2.base , group.cv = gcpo.default.3.base)


------------------------------------ The problem  ------------------------------------

When computing U(LGOCV, I get:

-mean(log(gcpo.ZIP1.bym2..iid.base$cv)) returns  NA
-mean(log(gcpo.ZIP0.bym2..iid.base$cv)) returns  0.3774887

-mean(log(gcpo.ZIP1.bym2.rw2.base$cv)) returns NA
-mean(log(gcpo.ZIP0.bym2.rw2.base$cv)) returns  NA

I'm trying to understand why some of these cross-validation results return NA . Is it due to zero predictions, numerical issues, or something else related to the ZIP models or group structure?


------------------------------------ Model formulas ------------------------------------

formula.bym2.rw2.iid_intI_iid <- O ~
  f(ID, model = "bym2", graph = g_ePIMAD,hyper = hyper_bym,constr = T, scale.model = T)+
  f(Year_int,model="rw2",hyper = hyper_iid_rw,constr = T, scale.model = T)+
  f(Year_int_bis,model="iid",hyper = hyper_iid_rw,constr = T)+
  f(SPID.Year,model="iid",hyper = hyper_iid_rw,constr = T)


formula.bym2..iid <- O ~
  f(ID, model = "bym2", graph = g_ePIMAD,hyper = hyper_bym,constr = T, scale.model = T)+
  f(Year_int_bis,model="iid",hyper = hyper_iid_rw,constr = T)

ZIP1.bym2..iid.base <- inla(formula.bym2..iid,
                            family="zeroinflatedpoisson1",data=map,E=E,verbose = TRUE,
                            control.compute = control.compute, control.inla = control.inla)


ZIP0.bym2..iid.base <- inla(formula.bym2..iid,
                            family="zeroinflatedpoisson0",data=map,E=E,verbose = TRUE,
                            control.compute = control.compute,control.inla = control.inla)


formula.bym2.rw2 <- O ~
  f(ID, model = "bym2", graph = g_ePIMAD,hyper = hyper_bym,constr = T, scale.model = T)+
  f(Year_int,model="rw2",hyper = hyper_iid_rw,constr = T, scale.model = T)

ZIP1.bym2.rw2.base <- inla(formula.bym2.rw2,
                           family="zeroinflatedpoisson1",data=map,E=E,verbose = TRUE,
                           control.compute = control.compute, control.inla = control.inla)



  Thanks in advance for any help or suggestions!

messages.author: 9a89594e7fcb7aad
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Why does inla.group.cv() return NA for some zero-inflated Poisson models?
parts:
if the response y is NA at some places, that corresponding 'cv' will be NA, but
it does not seems to be the acse here.

gcpo.default.3.base

will return a list and you can check $mean and $sd which is the latent mean and
sd without the data in the group, which is used to compute the cv. check if
anything is weird, where the cv-score is reported to be NA.

(I assume you're on R-4.5 and the most recent testing version...)
